extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural/formatting requirements for filing and prosecuting U.S. patent reissue applications (including related requirements for plant patents, publication, petitions, and Director actions). Covers who may apply, content and amendment rules, oath/declaration content, examination treatment, and ancillary procedures (publication/nonpublication, petitions, suspensions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant patent claim formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim shall be in formal terms to the new and distinct variety of the specified plant as described and illustrated, and may also recite the principal distinguishing characteristics. More than one claim is not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to plant patent claims: single claim only; must formally claim the new distinct variety and may include principal distinguishing characteristics (see § 1.164).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant patent drawings quality and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Plant patent drawings should be artistically and competently executed and must comply with the requirements of § 1.84. The drawing must disclose all the distinctive characteristics of the plant capable of visual representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: View numbers and reference characters need not be employed unless required by the examiner. Drawings must meet § 1.84 formalities and show all visually representable distinctive traits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant patent color drawing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawings may be in color. The drawing must be in color if color is a distinguishing characteristic of the new variety. Two copies of color drawings or photographs must be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Color is permissive unless it is a distinguishing feature, in which case color drawings/photos are required and must be submitted in two copies (see § 1.165(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant specimen availability requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may be required to furnish specimens of the plant, or its flower or fruit, in a quantity and at a time in its stage of growth as may be designated, for study and inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specimens must be properly packed and forwarded per instructions; if forwarding is not possible, plants must be made available for official inspection where grown (see § 1.166).

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral for agricultural examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications may be submitted by the Patent and Trademark Office to the Department of Agriculture for study and report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plant patent applications (and related matters) may be referred to USDA for technical study as part of examination (see § 1.167).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue application required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for reissue must contain the same parts required for an application for an original patent, complying with all the rules relating thereto, and in addition, must comply with the requirements of the rules relating to reissue applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, the entire specification including the claims and the drawings of the patent must be furnished (copy of printed patent in double-column format), and copies of any disclaimer, certificate of correction, or reexamination certificate issued in the patent must be included (see § 1.171 and § 1.173(a)). No new matter may be introduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may be reissue applicant and assignee consent
rubrics_metrics.description: The reissue applicant is the original patentee, or the current patent owner if there has been an assignment. A reissue application must be accompanied by the written consent of all assignees currently owning an undivided interest in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All assignees consenting must establish ownership by filing the required submission (e.g., per § 3.73). A reissue will be granted to the original patentee, legal representatives, or assigns as their interest may appear (see § 1.172).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue specification and drawing copy requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The entire specification, including the claims, of the patent for which reissue is requested must be furnished in the form of a copy of the printed patent, in double column format, each page on only one side of a single sheet of paper. Applicant must submit a clean copy of each drawing sheet of the printed patent at filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the drawing copy complies with § 1.84, no further drawings required. The Office will not transfer drawings from the patent file to the reissue application; copies of certain issued certificates/disclaimers must be included (see § 1.173(a)(1)-(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on new matter in reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: No new matter shall be introduced into the reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue must be limited to correcting errors in the existing patent; introducing new subject matter is not allowed (see § 1.173(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for making amendments in a reissue application
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment in a reissue application is made either by physically incorporating the changes into the specification when the application is filed, or by a separate amendment paper. If incorporation is used, markings pursuant to paragraph (d) must be used. If amendment is by amendment paper, the paper must direct specified changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two allowed methods: marked incorporation at filing (with underlining/bracketing) or separate amendment paper describing exact changes. Follow the specific subrules for types of content amended (specification paragraphs; large tables; program listing; sequence listings) (see § 1.173(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amending the specification (text) in reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to the specification, other than to the claims, must be made by submission of the entire text of an added or rewritten paragraph, including markings pursuant to paragraph (d), except that an entire paragraph may be deleted by a statement deleting the paragraph without presentation of the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must identify the precise point where any added or rewritten paragraph is located; follow special rules for large tables, program listings, and sequence listings (see § 1.173(b)(1)(i)-(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim amendment requirements in reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment paper must include the entire text of each claim being changed by such amendment paper and of each claim being added by such amendment paper. For any claim changed, a parenthetical expression "amended," "twice amended," etc., should follow the claim number. Changed and added claims must include markings pursuant to paragraph (d), except that a patent claim or added claim may be canceled by a statement canceling the claim without presentation of the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When altering claims in reissue, present full claim texts, mark their status with parentheticals, and use underlining/bracketing markings per the rule. Claims may not be renumbered; added claims must follow numbering after highest original patent claim (see § 1.173(b)(2) and (e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing amendment procedure for reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: Any changes to a patent drawing must be submitted as a replacement sheet of drawings which shall be an attachment to the amendment document. Replacement sheet must be in compliance with § 1.84 and include all figures appearing on the original sheet, even if only one figure is amended. Amended figures must be identified as "Amended," added as "New," and canceled figures bracketed and identified as "Canceled."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All changes to drawings must be explained in detail on a separate sheet. A marked-up annotated copy labeled "Annotated Marked-up Drawings" may be included and must be provided when required by the examiner (see § 1.173(b)(3)(i)-(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim status and support for claim changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever there is an amendment to the claims, there must be supplied, on pages separate from the pages containing the changes, the status (i.e., pending or canceled), as of the date of the amendment, of all patent claims and of all added claims, and an explanation of the support in the disclosure of the patent for the changes made to the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear claim status list and a support explanation to show basis in the original disclosure for each change (see § 1.173(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking convention for changes in reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: The matter to be omitted by reissue must be enclosed in brackets; and the matter to be added by reissue must be underlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Markings apply to specification and claims (excluding certain large tables and listings per the rule) and are mandatory when changes are made by incorporation or amendment paper (see § 1.173(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of patent claim numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent claims may not be renumbered. The numbering of any claim added in the reissue application must follow the number of the highest numbered patent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain original claim numbers; added claims must continue numbering after the highest original patent claim number (see § 1.173(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office-requested amendment for correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure must be amended, when required by the Office, to correct inaccuracies of description and definition, and to secure substantial correspondence between the claims, the remainder of the specification, and the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Office determines inconsistencies exist, applicant must amend the disclosure to align claims, specification, and drawings (see § 1.173(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor's oath/declaration requirements for reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor’s oath or declaration for a reissue application must, in addition to complying with other oath requirements, specifically identify at least one error pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 251 being relied upon as the basis for reissue and state that the applicant believes the original patent to be wholly or partly inoperative or invalid by reason of a defective specification or drawing, or by reason of the patentee claiming more or less than the patentee had the right to claim in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reissue seeks to enlarge claim scope, the oath/declaration must identify a claim sought to be broadened. The oath/declaration must be executed by each inventor or, in certain circumstances, by an assignee per the rule; supplemental oaths required if errors not previously covered are corrected (see § 1.175). Variations exist for pre-AIA filings (see § 1.175 (pre-AIA)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing reissue application oath reuse conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement for the inventor’s oath or declaration for a continuing reissue application that claims benefit of an earlier-filed reissue application may be satisfied by a copy of the oath/declaration from the earlier-filed reissue application provided specified conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions include that the inventor executed an oath in the earlier reissue, the continuing reissue does not seek to enlarge claims, or the original patent was filed under § 1.46 by the assignee of the entire interest; if all errors previously identified are no longer relied upon, a new identifying error must be provided (see § 1.175(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of reissue applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissue application will be examined in the same manner as a non-reissue, non-provisional application, and will be subject to all requirements of the rules related to non-reissue applications. Applications for reissue will be acted on by the examiner in advance of other applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restriction between subject matter of the original patent claims and previously unclaimed subject matter may be required; if restriction required, original patent claims will be held constructively elected unless a disclaimer of all the patent claims is filed (see § 1.176).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple reissue applications rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant files more than one application for the reissue of a single patent, each such application must contain in the first sentence of the specification a notice stating that more than one reissue application has been filed and identifying each reissue application by relationship, application number and filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each claim of the patent being reissued must be presented in each reissue application as amended, unamended, or canceled with the same claim numbers. The same claim may not be presented in its original unamended form for examination in more than one of the multiple reissue applications. The Office may suspend action, merge applications, or refuse issuance of an application that contains only unamended claims and does not correct an error (see § 1.177).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of filing a reissue application on original patent
rubrics_metrics.description: The application for reissue of a patent shall constitute an offer to surrender that patent, and the surrender shall take effect upon reissue of the patent. Until a reissue application is granted, the original patent shall remain in effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must call to the Office’s attention any prior or concurrent proceedings (interferences, PTAB trials, reexaminations, litigations) involving the patent and the results of such proceedings (see § 1.178).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to the Director—grounds and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Petition may be taken to the Director from any action or requirement of any examiner in ex parte prosecution (or certain reexamination proceedings) not subject to appeal to the PTAB; in cases where statute or rules specify Director review; or to invoke supervisory authority of the Director in appropriate circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions involving PTAB actions follow part 41. Petitions must set forth facts, points for review, requested action, and should include briefs/memoranda and proof (affidavits/declarations) where facts are to be proven (see § 1.181(a)-(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition procedural requirements (reconsideration, fees, timeliness, hearings)
rubrics_metrics.description: When petitioning from an examiner action, it may be required that there have been a proper request for reconsideration (§ 1.111) and a repeated action by the examiner. Fees indicated by the relevant rules must accompany petitions or they will be dismissed. Any petition not filed within two months of mailing of the action or notice may be dismissed as untimely (two-month period not extendable). Oral hearing will not be granted except when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a petition does not stay reply periods or other proceedings. The Director may delegate petition determinations to appropriate PTO officials; examiners may be directed to furnish written statements of reasons for their decisions (see § 1.181(c)-(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Director discretion for situations not covered
rubrics_metrics.description: All situations not specifically provided for in the regulations will be decided in accordance with the merits by or under the authority of the Director, subject to such other requirements as may be imposed; petitions under this section must be accompanied by the petition fee set forth in § 1.17(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director’s written decisions will be communicated to interested parties (see § 1.182).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension or waiver of non-statutory rules
rubrics_metrics.description: In an extraordinary situation, when justice requires, any requirement of the regulations which is not a requirement of the statutes may be suspended or waived by the Director or the Director’s designee, sua sponte, or on petition of the interested party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any petition under this section must be accompanied by the petition fee set forth in § 1.17(f) and is subject to such other requirements as may be imposed (see § 1.183).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing and exceptions for patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Each U.S. national application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) and each international application under 35 U.S.C. 371 will be published promptly after 18 months from the earliest filing date for which a benefit is sought unless: the application is no longer pending; is nationally security classified/under secrecy order; has issued as a patent in sufficient time; or was filed with a compliant nonpublication request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional, certain design, and reissue applications are not published under this section. Publication may be delayed until required filing elements (fees, translations, compliant specification, abstract, drawings, sequence listings, oath/ADS) are present. The Office may refuse publication or parts thereof that would violate law or contain offensive/disparaging material (see § 1.211).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication fee and payment timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The publication fee must be paid in each application published under this section before the patent will be granted. The sum specified in the notice of allowance will include the publication fee which must be paid within three months from the date of mailing of the notice of allowance to avoid abandonment; this three-month period is not extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application is not published, any paid publication fee will be refunded (see § 1.211(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpublication request requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonpublication request will prevent publication under 35 U.S.C. 122(b) if: a request is submitted with the application upon filing; the request states conspicuously that the application is not to be published; the request contains a certification that the invention has not been and will not be the subject of an application filed in another country (or under a multilateral agreement) that requires 18-month publication; and the request is signed in compliance with § 1.33(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant may rescind a nonpublication request at any time; failure to comply with the certification (e.g., later filing abroad) can have consequences under statutory rules (see § 1.213).
